newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Copper swamped by sales, more falls seen.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Copper swamped by sales, more falls seen.

text.p: Copper prices on the London Metal Exchange (LME) fell under a deluge of selling on Wednesday, and a rocky market is vulnerable to further decline, traders and analysts said.
Market sentiment has become increasingly sour in recent sessions, with metal stocks rising and demand slowing down for summer.
"If the market is going to turn, then this is the time of the year when it should be turning," Angus MacMillan of LME trader Billiton Metals said.
For some time many copper observers have expected the market to turn lower, with the weight of supply from a host of new mines outpacing demand growth.
On the LME, speculative selling intensified from Tuesday evening onwards, triggering sell-stops and option delta hedge selling before some semblance of stability returned.
But this pause, with prices some $20 above the lows, may only reflect bottom-picking.
"It does not look good at all...and it tends to get sold off late because you can move it in low volume in New York," one floor trader said.

Three months copper prices hit 4-1/2 month lows of $2,240 a tonne at point, well down from Tuesday's closing levels of $2,368. More significantly, the market is now some $340, or nearly 14 percent below the year's highs of $2,609 hit a month ago.
"The bulls have been fighting a rearguard battle," said MacMillan.
Although U.S. demand is slowing, copper bulls were pinning their hopes on China taking up the slack, but the Chinese are now selling metal, he noted.
And recent data issued by the International Copper Study Group (ICSG) shows that the market was more or less balanced during the first part of the year, MacMillan said.
Jan/April copper consumption was 4.406 million tonnes, against total refined production of 4.377 million tonnes, the ICSG figures show.
So market sentiment has turned negative because demand slows in the summer when consumer plant vacations result in reduced metal unit requirements, while most producers work around the clock.
This will result in stockpiles rising, and recent LME warehouse inventory data indicates that a stock uptrend is now in place.
LME stocks have risen 4,475 tonnes this week, after three successive daily increases, and arrivals are seen accelerating in coming weeks.

LME floor traders expect copper to be delivered into the U.S. stores at Long Beach and Los Angeles, into Rotterdam and Helsingborg in Europe, and in Singapore in the Far East, due to shipments from China, Taiwan, and South Korea.
Because sentiment is so shaky, a total stoppage at Portugal's Neves Corvo mine is being ignored.
"This affects copper concentrate availability, but there is plenty of cathode likely to be around," one trader noted.
In the short-term, significant price declines may be put on hold, due to the technical tightness that exists for copper in the second half of July on the LME and subsequent steep backwardations.
But there are signs that they are easing also, with the benchmark cash/threes backwardation at $118/25 on Wednesday, against levels of $150 at the start of the week.
"This price is going to be a lot lower in the long-term, but there is an awful lot of trading to be done before then," one trader said.
--London newsroom 44 171 542 8080
